questions.explanation:
Given,

$\cos \left({\sin }^{ - 1}\left(x\cot \left({\tan }^{ - 1}\left(\cos \left({\sin }^{ - 1}x\right)\right)\right)\right)\right) = k$

Now simplifying $\cos \left({\sin }^{ - 1}x\right) = \cos \left({\cos }^{ - 1}\sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}}\right) = \sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}}$

So, $\cos \left({\sin }^{ - 1}\left(x\cot \left({\tan }^{ - 1}\left(\cos \left({\sin }^{ - 1}x\right)\right)\right)\right)\right) = k$

becomes $\cos \left({\sin }^{ - 1}\left(x\cot \left({\tan }^{ - 1}\sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}}\right)\right)\right) = k$

And now solving $\cot \left({\tan }^{ - 1}\sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}}\right) = {\mathrm{cotcot}}^{ - 1}\left(\sqrt{\frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}}}}\right) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}}}$

So, $\cos \left({\sin }^{ - 1}\left(x\cot \left({\tan }^{ - 1}\sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}}\right)\right)\right) = k$ becomes

$\cos \left({\sin }^{ - 1}\left(\frac{x}{\sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}}}\right)\right) = k$

Now solving $\cos \left({\sin }^{ - 1}\left(\frac{x}{\sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}}}\right)\right) = \frac{\sqrt{1 - 2{x}^{2}}}{\sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}}}$

So, $\frac{\sqrt{1 - 2{x}^{2}}}{\sqrt{1 - {x}^{2}}} = k \implies 1 - 2{x}^{2} = {k}^{2}\left(1 - {x}^{2}\right) \implies \left({k}^{2} - 2\right){x}^{2} = {k}^{2} - 1 \implies {x}^{2} = \frac{{k}^{2} - 1}{{k}^{2} - 2}$

So, roots are $\alpha = \sqrt{\frac{{k}^{2} - 1}{{k}^{2} - 2}} \implies {\alpha }^{2} = \frac{{k}^{2} - 1}{{k}^{2} - 2}$

And $\beta = - \sqrt{\frac{{k}^{2} - 1}{{k}^{2} - 2}} \implies {\beta }^{2} = \frac{{k}^{2} - 1}{{k}^{2} - 2}$

Now finding $\frac{1}{{\alpha }^{2}} + \frac{1}{{\beta }^{2}} = 2\left(\frac{{k}^{2} - 2}{{k}^{2} - 1}\right)$ and $\frac{\alpha }{\beta } = - 1$

So, sum of roots of {x}^{2} - bx - 5 = 0$ will be $= \frac{1}{{\alpha }^{2}} + \frac{1}{{\beta }^{2}} + \frac{\alpha }{\beta } = b \implies \frac{2\left({k}^{2} - 2\right)}{{k}^{2} - 1} - 1 = b⋯\left(1\right)$

Product of roots of {x}^{2} - bx - 5 = 0$ will be $= \left(\frac{1}{{\alpha }^{2}} + \frac{1}{{\beta }^{2}}\right)\frac{\alpha }{\beta } = - 5 \implies \frac{2\left({k}^{2} - 2\right)}{{k}^{2} - 1}\left( - 1\right) = - 5 \implies 2{k}^{2} - 4 = 5{k}^{2} - 5 \implies 3{k}^{2} = 1 \implies {k}^{2} = \frac{1}{3}⋯\mathrm{Put}\mathrm{in}\left(1\right) \implies b = \frac{2\left({k}^{2} - 2\right)}{{k}^{2} - 1} - 1 = 5 - 1 = 4 \frac{b}{{k}^{2}} = \frac{4}{\frac{1}{3}} = 12$

questions.explanation:
Given,

{\sin }^{ - 1}\left(\frac{x + 1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2} + 2x + 2}}\right) - {\sin }^{ - 1}\left(\frac{x}{\sqrt{{x}^{2} + 1}}\right) = \frac{\pi }{4} \implies {\sin }^{ - 1}\left(\frac{x + 1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2} + x + 2}}\right) = \frac{\pi }{4} + {\sin }^{ - 1}\frac{x}{\sqrt{{x}^{2} + 1}} \implies \left(\frac{x + 1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2} + x + 2}}\right) = \sin \left(\frac{\pi }{4} + {\sin }^{ - 1}\frac{x}{\sqrt{{x}^{2} + 1}}\right) \implies \left(\frac{x + 1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2} + x + 2}}\right) = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2} + 1}} + \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \times \frac{x}{\sqrt{{x}^{2} + 1}} \implies \frac{x + 1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2} + x + 2}} = \frac{x + 1}{\sqrt{2}\sqrt{{x}^{2} + 1}} \implies \left(x + 1\right)\left(\sqrt{2}\sqrt{{x}^{2} + 1} - \sqrt{{x}^{2} + x + 2}\right) = 0 \implies x = - 1$ or $\sqrt{{x}^{2} + x + 2} = \sqrt{2} \cdot \sqrt{{x}^{2} + 1}$

Now solving, $\sqrt{{x}^{2} + x + 2} = \sqrt{2} \cdot \sqrt{{x}^{2} + 1}$ we get,

{x}^{2} + x + 2 = 2\left({x}^{2} + 1\right) \implies {x}^{2} - x = 0 \implies x = 0,x = 1$ {rejected as $x = 1$ will not satisfy the given equation}

Hence, $S = \left(0,1\right)$

Now solving,

$\underset{n \in S}{ \sum }\left(\sin \left({x}^{2} + x + 5\right)\frac{\pi }{2} - \cos \left({x}^{2} + x + 5\right)\pi \right) = \left(\sin \frac{5\pi }{2} - \cos 5\pi + \sin \frac{5\pi }{2} - \cos 5\pi \right) = 1 - \left( - 1\right) + 1 - \left( - 1\right) = 4$
